title: Russian Internal Fragility Deepens as Fuel Crisis Bites Into Autumn
statement: Russia's forced shift to sea-borne gasoline imports (India/Morocco/Turkey) plus regional rationing and 70+ refinery strikes signals a structural war-economy fragility that will deepen through autumn. A fuel-rationed Russia under ongoing strategic-strike pressure becomes a more unpredictable and desperate regional actor, raising risk of escalatory behavior as it enters winter — an unreliable domestic baseline eroding the regime's capacity to sustain the war while managing internal stability.
evidence_confirmed: Putin admitted 'We Were Mistaken' (Sept 3, 2026): Russia assumed refineries were untargetable civilian facilities.
70+ Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries since Jan 2026; refining output at lowest in two decades.
Gasoline covers ~70% of domestic demand (30k ton/day shortfall); 17 regions rationing fuel (caps, odd-even).
Russia importing gasoline by sea from India, Morocco, Turkey; record purchases from Belarus; KINEF (2nd-largest refinery) stopped processing Sept 2.
2026-09-08: Urals fell to $59, Russia's oil revenue sinking as fuel crunch deepens globally (Oilprice.com).
falsifier: Russian refining recovers (KINEF restart, imports fall, rationing ends, output target met) AND domestic stability holds through winter - the regime demonstrates it can absorb the strategic-strike degradation without acute internal crisis or desperate external escalation.
forward_watchlist: KINEF restart + refining-throughput recovery - the recovery baseline.
Autumn/winter rationing expansion vs. relaxation; regional unrest over fuel/cold (internal-fragility transmission).
Continued Ukrainian strike tempo (sustained degradation) vs. negotiation-induced pause.
Any Russian escalatory act born of desperation (Baltic probe, sanctions-breaking, nuclear signaling) as fragility external shadow.
Sea-borne gasoline import dependency - the seam of the crisis.
